# Public API

Edited Wednesday, November 12 2025

Fathom now has a public API that gives you developer‑friendly access to meeting insights so you can build workflows and integrations that connect Fathom with the rest of your tools.

  * Build exactly what you need - bring meeting summaries, transcripts, and action items right into your own tools and workflows for a tailored experience.

  * Save time with automation - automate repetitive post‑meeting tasks and cut out manual copy‑paste so work moves faster.

  * Unlock more use cases - extend Fathom with third‑party apps and integrations, opening the door to new org‑wide use cases.

### Who this is for

  * Anyone can browse the API docs and start building!

  * Partners can register an OAuth app to be eligible for a future marketplace listing as a Fathom‑approved integration.

### How to get started

  * Looking for plug‑and‑play integrations? Visit the Integration Hub.

  * Building internal workflows? Start with the Quickstart Guide.

  * Publishing an integration for customers? Create an OAuth app here.

### Keep in mind

  * API keys and access: API keys are created at the user level. Your key can access meetings recorded by you or shared to your Team. Admin API keys do not grant access to other users’ unshared meetings.

  * Rate Limiting: users can make 60 calls per minute across all of their API keys; this ensures system stability and reliability. With that in mind, we do not offer higher rate limits at this time.

If you have any questions, reach out to help@fathom.video. We’re happy to assist!

# Calling Fathom’s Integration API Programmatically

## Prerequisites

Before you can access the Fathom Integration API programmatically, you’ll need to contact Fathom to obtain:

  * Client ID – Your unique application identifier
  * Client Secret – Your application’s secret key (keep this secure!)
  * API Hostname – The specific hostname for your Fathom instance

Please confirm your exact hostname with Fathom, as it may vary based on your deployment. Also, depending on the security requirements of your enterprise deployment, additional criteria might be necessary to enable access across the firewall.

## Getting an API Access Token

Before making API calls, you need to obtain an OAuth2 access token using your client credentials.

### Python Example
    
    `import requests
    
    def get_access_token():
        """
        Obtain an OAuth2 access token using client credentials.
        Returns the access token string.
        """
        # Replace {your-instance} with your actual hostname
        auth_url = "https://auth.{your-instance}.fathom.one/oauth2/token"

## Calling the GraphQL API

Once you have an access token, you can make GraphQL queries to the Fathom Integration API.

### Python Example

    def make_api_call(access_token: str, query: str, variables: dict):
        """
        Execute a GraphQL query against the Fathom Integration API.
        
        Args:
            access_token: OAuth2 access token
            query: GraphQL query string
            variables: Dictionary of query variables
        
        Returns:
            The data response from the API
        """
        # Replace {your-instance} with your actual hostname
        api_url = "https://{your-instance}.fathom.one/api/integrations"
        
        headers = {
            "content-type": "application/json",
            "authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}"
        }
        
        payload = [
            {
                "variables": variables,
                "query": query,
            }
        ]
        
        response = requests.post(api_url, headers=headers, json=payload)

## Important Notes

  1. Keep your credentials secure: Never commit your `client_id` or `client_secret` to version control. Use environment variables or secure configuration management.

  2. Token reuse and expiration: Fathom requires that you reuse access tokens until they expire. Do NOT request a new token for every API call. Store the access token and use it for multiple requests until it expires, then request a new one. Implement token refresh logic in production applications that checks expiration before making requests.

  3. Error handling: Always check for both HTTP errors and GraphQL errors in the response.

  4. Rate limiting: Be mindful of API rate limits. Implement appropriate retry logic with exponential backoff for production use.

  5. User-Agent header: The `user-agent` header helps Fathom identify and support your integration. It may be required depending on the security configuration for your deployment.

For more information about available queries and the GraphQL schema, see the GraphQL Documentation.

For API updates and version history, see the API Release Notes.

# Start a trial

The first step in starting a subscription is to sign up for a free 14-day trial of Fathom.

The trial is fully functional, and no billing information is required. You can add data from as many companies as you want, invite unlimited users, and generate as many reports as you need.

We also provide a demo company to view our analysis, reports, and forecasting tools without importing your own data. This demo company can be found at the bottom of the 'My Companies' page or the main Fathom home screen.

💡Smart Tip: While the demo company provides insight into how some of Fathom's features work, not all features are shown in the demo company, and the Forecasting area of the demo company is limited in functionality. You'll get the best idea of Fathom and its features by importing your own data.

Python REST

The SDK performs the obtaining of tokens for the user when creating a Client object. Just use the access credentials supplied by Fathom.
    
    `from fathom.sdk.v2 import Client
    
    client = Client(
        "client_id",
        "client_secret",
    )
    
    # Future requests will be authenticated
    `

To access data from the REST API endpoints you will need to authorize requests using a JWT token in the `Authorization` header. To be able to do this, you must obtain a token from our authorization server using your supplied `client_id` and `client_secret`.
    
    `curl --request POST \
      --url https://api.fathom.global/v2/auth/token \
      --header 'content-type: application/json' \
      --data '{"client_id":"CLIENT_ID","client_secret":"CLIENT_SECRET"}'
    `

You should obtain a response like:
    
    `{
      "access_token": "access_token",
      "expire_secs": 86400
    }
    `

When you have the Auth0 JWT token you will need to pass it as a header with every request to any of the Fathom API endpoints using the pattern:
    
    `Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN
    `
